full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Miftah Uddin Chowdhury, J:-This Rule arises out of the judgment and decree dated 15.06.1999 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong; in Other Appeal No.305 .of 1981, affirming those dated 29.07.1981 passed by the learned Sub Ordinate Judge, Third Court, Chittagong, in Other Suit No.28 of 1973. 

 2. The opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted the suit impleading Late Sreemati Khulana Bala Chowdhury. the predecessor of the petitioner and the Government of Bangladesh as defendant Nos. l and 2 respectively for a decree of Specific Performance of Contract starting that the defendant No.1 Srimati Khulana Bala Chowdhurani was the owner and possessor of the suit land. Being in need of money to meet her necessity of reconstructing her dwelling huts she entered into a contract with him (plaintiff) to sell the suit land at a consideration of Taka 16.537.50 and executed a Bainapatra on 10.07.1972 in favour of him on receipt of Taka 2,001.00 as advance in consultation with her son-in-law Mr. Sunirmal Chandra Das. As per the said 13ainapatra the plaintiff supposed to obtain necessary permission and certificates from the concern authorities within next six months and on payment of the rest amount by him the Kabala was supposed to be executed and registered by the defendant No.1 otherwise it will be cancelled and the earnest money will be forfeited. He is a businessman and used to reside in Dhaka and Mymensing and his affairs in Chittagong are usually looked after by his material uncle Mr. Nurul Alam. On 24.12.1972 the son-in-law of the defendant No.1 approached before the said maternal uncle of him for making arrangement to pay a further amount of Taka 5,000.00 out of the balance consideration, accordingly the said uncle on 28.12.1972 made payment of further amount of Taka 3,000.00 in presence of Mr. Mustafa Kamal and Mr. Taslim Uddin. On 28.01.1973 while he was staying in Mymensing received a notice dated 28.01.1973 from the defendant No.1 through her lawyer demanding the balance of the consideration within next seven days. The said notice contains some untrue statements about the responsibility of obtaining necessary permission. Since he was otherwise busy it was impossible on his part to come Chittagong immediately. On 01.02.1973 he replied the said notice asking for further time of one month to complete the transaction. In the mean time through his maternal uncle on 04.02.1973 he sent the rest of amount to the defendant No.1 and requested her to execute and register the Kabala but she was not in possession to execute the Kabala since she could not obtain the necessary permission and certificate. Ultimately she denied to execute an register the Kabala and hence the suit. 1 The suit was contested by the defendant No.1 by filing written statement admitting the execution of Bainapatra with further statement that as per the Bainapatra the plaintiff was bound to make payment of the rest amount within six months from the date of execution of the Bainapatra. She proposed to sell the suit land for her urgent need which need was nothing but construction of her dwelling huts since her dwelling huts were destroyed. The plaintiff paid a poor amount of Taka 2,000.00 and thereafter he did not make payment of the rest within time stipulated in the Bainapatra. Since she was in problem with her dwelling huts she by selling her other properties constructed her dwelling huts. For non payment of the rest of the consideration money within the time stipulated in the Bainapatra the earnest money had already been forfeited and the Bainapatra has already became unenforceable and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. After hearing the parties the Trial Court decreed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29.07.1981. On appeal it was affirmed by the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.06.1999 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong, in Other Appeal No.305 of 1981. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the petitioner as successor of the original defendant No.1 moved this Court in revision and obtained the Rule. 

 6. Mr. Shishir Kanti Majumder, Advocate, appearing for the petitioner placed the judgment of the Courts below from which it is apparent that both the Courts below did not believe the story of making payment of further amount of Taka 3,000.00 by the plaintiff through his maternal uncle, rather the Courts below found that the said story is false. Even after such finding, the Courts below decreed the suit. Mr. Majumder further submits that the judgment and decree of the Courts below are not maintainable in the eye of law though based on concurrent findings of fact. Mr. Majumder placed the provision of law provides in sub-section 2 of Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act. As per the said provision of law granting a decree in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract is a discretionary relief. This sort of discretionary relief should be granted after considering the facts and circumstances of the case. He further submits that it is apparent that the plaintiff did not approach the Court for such relief with clean hand, rather the plaintiff approach the Court with concocted story of making further payment through his 'maternal uncle. Moreover, since the plaintiff did not make payment of the balance of the consideration within the stipulated time the defendant No.1 compelled to sell her other properties to construct her dwelling huts and if the decree passed by the Courts below is maintained the defendant will loss her another property. In the instant case, even after expiry of six months the defendant No.1 by a notice requested the plaintiff to make payment of the rest amount, but the plaintiff did not make such payment, rather purposely make a concocted story of payment of further amount through his maternal uncle which was found as false by the Courts below. He further submits a person like the plaintiff who did not approach the Court with clean hand 

 can not be entitled for decree of Specific Performance of Contract in a suit like the instant one. He further submits in granting the decree the Courts below illegally misinterpreted the terms of the contract. On perusal of the deed of contract it is apparent that, it was the duty of the plaintiff to obtain the necessary permission and to make payment within next six months. But the Courts below on misinterpretation of the terms of contract decreed the suit illegally which occasioned failure of justice. In support, cited the decisions in the case of, Tajul Islam (Md.) Vs. Siraj Miah reported in 3 BLC (IICD) 393, Dewan Abul Abbas Vs. Muna Haque and others reported in 57 DLR (HC) 310, Rakhal Dasi Rajakini Vs. Ayesha Khatun Chowdhury and another reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 49 and Md. Lutfar Rahman and others Vs. Golam Ahmed Shah and others reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 231. 

 7. Mr. Mostafa Kamal Pasha, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party submits a Counter Affidavit which contains nothing but some statements supporting the impugned judgment and decree. In the oral submission he tried to support the impugned judgment. 

 8. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the record and I have also gone through the decisions cited above. On perusal of record it appears to me that the courts below did not exercise their discretion in judicial manner. In deciding the suit the Courts below failed to find that the plaintiff did not approach the Court with clean hand rather he approached the Court with some false concocted story which• was disbelieved. When the Courts below disbelieved such story they committed illegality in decreeing the suit. In the instant ease out of Tk.16,537.50 only an amount of Tk. 2.000.00 was paid by the plaintiff an earnest money to get the Bainapatra. As per the Bainapatra the plaintiff supposed to pay further amount of Tk.14,537.50 within next six months, otherwise the Bainapatra would be unenforceable. Apparently the plaintiff failed to make such payment within the stipulated time though after expiry of that time the defendant No.1 allowed him further seven days. In such situation I hold the view that for execution of Bainapatra a seller can not wait for unlimited time to sell the land to the person on whose behalf she or he executed the Bainapatra. The seller used to sell the land for his/her necessity. Waiting for unlimited time will never meet such necessity. In the instant case the defendant No.1 executed the Bainapatra to sell her property to meet up the expense of constructing her dwelling huts which was not possible by Taka 2,000.00 only and as such for meeting her necessity she sold her other properties. In such circumstances the plaintiff is not entitled to get any discretionary relief like the decree in such suit for specific performance of contract. 

 9. In the result, the Rule is hereby made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.06.1999 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong and those dated 29.07.1981 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, Third Court, Chittagong, in Other Suit No.28 of 1973 are hereby set aside.
